sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Nickel downstreaming in Indonesia will sustain long-term demand as global EV battery supply chains lock in processing capacity, despite near-term price volatility.
Copper's structural deficit, driven by electrification and renewable energy infrastructure, supports pricing power for producers like FCX and local beneficiaries.
Coal faces regulatory and environmental headwinds, but domestic energy security needs and export diversification to Asia keep the sector relevant for the next 3-5 years.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's mining sector shows mild divergence with US strength, but local laggards signal caution. Focus on ALKA's surge and FCX's copper exposure as tactical plays; avoid chasing INPS without volume confirmation. Structural demand for nickel and copper remains intact, but regulatory overhang on coal and gold persists.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Geothermal expansion remains Indonesia's most durable renewable driver due to baseload reliability and government targets for 7.2 GW by 2030, with BREN positioned as a key beneficiary.
Hydrogen's global momentum, reflected in PLUG's surge, could catalyze Indonesia's green hydrogen pilot projects, but infrastructure gaps limit near-term scalability.
US climate-tech outperformance (CEG, VST) highlights capital flow divergence, pressuring Indonesia to accelerate project financing reforms to attract similar investment.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables lag (-0.47%) vs US gains (+0.26%) signals domestic policy execution risk, but PLUG +6.57% and BREN +3.43% show selective momentum in hydrogen and geothermal. Favor BREN for Indonesia's baseload geothermal mandate; avoid 051910 until regulatory clarity on solar tariffs emerges.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG

sectors.ai: Buy ZATA and AGAR on strong volume spikes; both signal structural demand shifts in halal-certified snacks and agar-based FMCG. Trim US-exposed names like HAS and WMUU as ID consumer outperforms.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's mandatory JKN health insurance expansion is a durable driver, increasing formal-sector enrollment and boosting demand for hospital services and generic drugs.
Government push for domestic pharmaceutical self-sufficiency, including API production and tax incentives, creates long-term moats for local manufacturers.
Aging population and rising non-communicable disease prevalence structurally lift demand for chronic care, diagnostics, and private health insurance penetration.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's healthcare sector remains a defensive laggard with a slight aggregate dip, but global movers like UNH and LLY signal resilient demand for managed care and pharma innovation. For Indonesia, focus on domestic policy catalysts—JKN expansion and local manufacturing incentives—to drive structural growth, while global biotech tailwinds support selective exposure to multinationals with local partnerships.
